name: Genuit Group plc
executive_summary:
Genuit Group plc is the UK’s largest supplier of sustainable water and climate products for the built environment (Polypipe, Nuaire, Adey and related brands), pursuing a “Sustainable Solutions for Growth” strategy through organic share gains, regulatory tailwinds and bolt-on M&A. The quantitative screen rates GEN.L a **Strong Buy** (8/22 models; composite 79%), anchored on cheapness (P/B 1.15, FCF yield 7.0%), dividend income (4.1% yield, progressive policy) and moderate leverage (D/E 38%), though ROE remains weak at 6.9%. Primary filings confirm a cash-generative, strategically coherent business—FY2025 revenue of £602.1m (+7.3%) and underlying operating profit of £94.4m (+2.4%) with 102% pre-capex cash conversion—but H1 2026 shows volume pressure (LFL revenue −4.8%) and margin compression from polymer inflation and Adey operational issues, with management reiterating full-year expectations unchanged. The central debate is whether structural drivers (AMP8, Future Homes Standard, ventilation regulation) and recent acquisitions (Monodraught, Davidson Holdings) will re-accelerate earnings before cyclical headwinds and elevated intangibles/leverage erode the value case.

---
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, Genuit presents a **quality-at-a-reasonable-price** profile rather than a deep distressed bargain. The screen passes four factor families—**cheapness, dividend, GARP and risk**—with full data coverage (20/20 metrics), suggesting the signal is not driven by missing inputs. Asset-based cheapness (Schloss Low P/B; P/B 1.15 vs book) sits alongside a 7.0% FCF yield and a progressive dividend (12.9p FY2025; interim maintained at 4.2p in H1 2026), while the Financial Health and Earnings Quality models pass despite cyclical end-markets.

Business quality supports the screen’s risk bucket: FY2025 underlying operating cash conversion was **102%** (filings), leverage **1.5×** pro-forma EBITDA (well inside the **<3.0×** covenant), and liquidity headroom was **£219.8m** at year-end. Management has demonstrated market outperformance in soft UK construction—FY2025 LFL revenue **+3.2%**—via share gains (e.g. drainage competitor exit), sustainability-led segments (ventilation, blue-green roofs) and disciplined M&A. The May 2026 trading update and August 2026 interim confirm acquisitions are integrating ahead of plan (Davidson >20% EBIT margin; Monodraught order intake >£2m/month).

The screen’s weak spot is **return on equity (6.9%)**, consistent with a goodwill-heavy balance sheet (goodwill **£509.6m**; negative tangible book per Yahoo fallback). Value investors must accept that earnings power, not liquidation value, drives the thesis—and that near-term earnings are being managed through price increases and cost simplification (£4m+ annualised savings targeted for 2027) against a challenging macro backdrop. The Strong Buy signal is therefore best read as **accumulate on valuation and cash/dividend attributes**, with conviction tempered until H2 2026 margin recovery is visible in filings.

**Divisional FY2025 (prior three-unit structure):** CMS revenue £178.9m (+10.7%; LFL +5.9%), margin 13.6%; WMS revenue £169.5m (+5.3%; LFL +0.5%), margin **5.7%** (H2 recovery to 6.7%); SBS revenue £246.8m (+6.5%; LFL +3.3%), margin **24.3%**. **M&A and capital allocation:** Monodraught (£55.6m EV, August 2025) and Davidson Holdings (£49.0m EV, September 2025) funded via existing facilities; both expected margin-accretive in 2026. RCF extended/increased to **£350.0m** through August 2028; covenants comfortably met (interest cover **9.7×** vs >4.0× requirement).

**Pensions:** Group has **no defined benefit schemes**—defined contribution only; pension costs **£9.1m** (FY2025).

Companies House group accounts (2022–2025 filings indexed; bodies available) provide statutory corroboration but the RNS preliminary results above are the primary consolidated source for FY2025.

**Two-division restated view:** Climate Division revenue £89.7m (+2.4%; LFL −8.1%), underlying margin **9.7%** (Adey slow-stock provision £1.5m and supplier quality failure £0.8m); Water Division revenue £217.3m (+4.1%; LFL −3.3%), underlying margin **16.2%** (Davidson businesses >20% margin). Management stated **full-year expectations unchanged** and guided FY cash conversion **>90%**.

**Non-underlying H1 2026:** £17.7m before tax (vs £7.1m prior year), including £4.9m restructuring, £4.0m IT/ERP transformation, £1.0m Polydeck disposal loss, £0.6m social-engineering fraud excess. Polydeck sold 31 March 2026.

### Trading update (four months to 30 April 2026 — RNS, 22 May 2026)

- Revenue **£198.5m** (−0.4% YoY; **LFL −8.7%**), impacted by wet weather (Jan–Feb), Middle East-linked polymer/freight inflation (from March) and soft UK sentiment.
- Double-digit price increases implemented May 2026; simplification targeting **£4m–£5m** annualised savings (majority benefit 2027).
- H1 underlying operating profit anticipated **~£44.6m** (in line with prior year reported); FY2026 underlying OP **towards lower end** of analyst consensus **£94.7m–£105.5m**, assuming conflict resolution and macro stabilisation.

### Multi-year trend (filings + Yahoo fallback)

Filings establish a clear post-rebrand trajectory: revenue recovered from Yahoo-reported **£561.3m (2024)** to **£602.1m (2025)** after a 2023 dip (**£586.5m** per Yahoo, not re-stated in current RNS bodies). Underlying profitability has grown modestly (**£92.2m → £94.4m**), but margins remain below peak as labour (National Insurance/NLW) and input-cost inflation bite. Net debt rose materially with FY2025 M&A (**£129.2m → £208.1m** per filings; Yahoo net debt ex-leases **£179.3m** at FY2025—slightly different definition). Free cash flow per Yahoo: **£72.9m (2025)** vs **£78.4m (2024)**—directionally consistent with filing cash conversion but not used as primary figures.

**Gap note:** No separate H1 or H2 2025 interim filing body is indexed; H1 2026 comparatives are embedded in the half-year RNS. Historical CH accounts pre-2025 provide statutory depth but lack the APM granularity of RNS releases.

risks_and_flags:
**Cyclical / macro:** UK new-build and RMI volumes remain subdued; H1 2026 LFL revenue **−4.8%**. Trading update cited wet weather, UK Budget uncertainty and Middle East conflict driving polymer and freight inflation. Middle East revenue (~3.5% of FY2025) was **~50% lower** YoY in the four months to April 2026.

**Operational / divisional:** WMS margins collapsed to **5.7%** in FY2025 (inventory provision in H1); Climate Division H1 2026 margin **9.7%** reflects Adey-specific stock and supplier issues. Underfloor heating and RMI heating remain structurally weak. Principal risks (referenced unchanged from 2025 ARA in interim) include macro-political conditions, raw material supply/pricing, key customer reliance, and recruitment/retention.

**Leverage / liquidity:** Leverage rose from **0.9× to 1.6×** post-acquisitions—still within covenants and **£209.1m** liquidity headroom at H1 2026, but de-leveraging is an stated priority. Interest cover remains comfortable (**9.7×** FY2025).

**M&A / intangibles / accounting:** Goodwill **£509.6m**; FY2024 Adey goodwill impairment **£12.4m** (no further impairment FY2025/H1 2026). Heavy non-underlying charges: restructuring, acquisition amortisation (**£13.7m** FY2025; **£6.9m** H1 2026), multi-year ERP/cloud transformation expensed as exceptional. Polydeck held-for-sale impairment and **£1.0m** disposal loss. Social-engineering fraud **£0.6m** (Middle East operation). Tangible book value negative per Yahoo (**−£10.1m** FY2025)—screen cheapness is not asset-liquidation based.

**Governance / regulatory:** No going-concern qualification; directors adopt going concern through **December 2027** with reverse stress testing. Defined benefit pension risk is **absent** (DC only). Regulatory tailwinds (AMP8, Future Homes Standard, Awaab’s Law) are opportunities but depend on government execution and construction pipeline recovery.

**Competitive:** Market share gains (drainage, Barratt Redrow) are positive but may be partly competitor-exit driven and not necessarily repeatable.

RiskTags: cyclical, competitive, leverage, accounting, other

research_rationale: Primary filings validate the screen’s cash generation, dividend sustainability and moderate-leverage profile and confirm strategic progress via acquisitions and regulatory positioning, but H1 2026 volume/margin pressure and weak ROE/intangible-heavy balance sheet prevent full confirmation of a frictionless Strong Buy.
